title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning to improve queueing fairness and prevent starvation with timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: The continuous batcher scheduler showed unfair queueing behavior under mixed workload profiles: long-lived high-token requests could monopolize batching slots and cause tail latency spikes or effective starvation for short, latency-sensitive requests. This PR tunes the scheduler heuristics and introduces timeout-based eviction and starvation-protection logic to improve fairness without regressing throughput.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduced a configurable fairness policy (fairness_policy=v2) that scores requests by a combination of waiting_time_ms, estimated_token_cost, and priority_hint. 2) Added per-request max_wait_ms and a batch_timeout_ms that will cut a pending batch to dispatch if waits exceed thresholds. 3) Starvation protection: requests that have been requeued > N times are bumped in score and will preempt low-priority pending work. 4) Backpressure and requeue jitter: when a batch fails to form due to capacity, requests are requeued with exponential backoff and randomized jitter to avoid thundering herds. 5) KV cache hot-key protection: requests hitting the same KV-cache shard are distributed across batches to avoid serialization. 6) New feature flag continuous_batcher.fairness_v2 and runtime knobs exposed in scheduler config for gradual rollout.

Implementation notes: The core scheduler changes live in services/continuous-batcher/scheduler.go and supporting utilities in services/continuous-batcher/score.go. Configuration parsing and feature flag checks are handled in pkg/config/flags.go. The KV-cache protection uses a lightweight tokenized shard hint (pkg/kvcache/shard_hint.go) added to request metadata; this is advisory for the scheduler. Unit tests cover scoring, timeout handling, and starvation bump logic. Integration bench harness in perf-canary/benchmarks/continuous-batcher was extended to simulate mixed latency/cost workloads.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on a 8-GPU test cluster (p3-equivalent) with mixed workload (70% short <64-token, 30% long >1024-token) show: - 95th percentile latency for short requests: reduced from 220ms -> 140ms (-36%). - Overall throughput (tokens/s): within 3% of baseline (within noise). - No measurable increase in median latency for long requests; 99th percentile for very long requests increased by ~4% under extreme synthetic contention. Canary rollout observed similar improvements.

Testing & CI: Added ~18 unit tests and 2 integration scenarios. CI initially showed a flaky test in perf-canary which was addressed by adding a deterministic seed for the requeue jitter test. All checks are green on merge.

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged under continuous_batcher.fairness_v2. We will rollout to 10% of traffic for 24h, then 50% for 48h, observing token-level latency and tail regressions. If a regression is detected, the flag can be disabled to revert behavior without a code rollback.

Risk & mitigations: The primary risk is small-batch throughput regression due to more aggressive preemption. Mitigation: conservative defaults (max_wait_ms=15ms, batch_timeout_ms=25ms) and the ability to tune in prod. We also included safe-guards to avoid infinite requeues and per-client throttling to prevent priority inversion.

Related work: Follow-up PRs will add telemetry dashboards and an A/B evaluation harness in redwood-console. References: ENG-3124 for design doc, ENG-3198 for benchmarking plan.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can you explain how the starvation bump avoids priority inversion if many bumped requests arrive concurrently?

Asha Patel (author): The bump includes a small randomized offset and a requeue_backoff_ms cap; bumped requests gain score but are still subject to the backpressure window so they cannot starve others indefinitely. Added explanation and a unit test that simulates concurrent bumps.
Leah Kim: The default max_wait_ms seems low for high variance workloads. How did you pick 15ms?

Asha Patel (author): We tuned defaults using the perf-canary trace traces from production; 15ms reduced tail for short requests without impacting throughput in our observed workloads. It's exposed as a config knob for operators to increase in noisy environments.
Owen Zhang: CI initially failed on a flaky jitter test — was that fixed?
Asha Patel (author): Yes, fixed by seeding the RNG and adding a small tolerance window; CI is green now.
Miguel Torres: Please add an entry in CHANGELOG highlighting the feature flag and config knobs for operators.
Asha Patel (author): Added CHANGELOG.md entry and docs/continuous-batcher.md section on rollout and tuning.
Leah Kim: Approved after addressing comments.
release_notes: Scheduler: introduce fairness_v2 scoring, per-request max_wait_ms and batch_timeout_ms, starvation protection and KV-cache shard advisory distribution. Feature-flagged and disabled by default. Operators: tune continuous_batcher.{max_wait_ms,batch_timeout_ms,starvation_threshold}.
